<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916678_theRebbe_290" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916678_theRebbe_290__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section raises a difficulty with the preceding concept.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And superficially, it is difficult:</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that we find nations of the world transgressing the Seven Noachide Laws they were commanded.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">A)</t>
    <t s="1">Behold, we find nations of the world transgressing the Seven Noachide Laws that they were commanded.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the simple resolution, drawing on the parallel with the Jewish people, that either a spirit of folly or the heart's dominance over the mind causes the transgression, contrary to their essential nature.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the simple resolution,</t>
    <t s="1">it is,</t>
    <t s="2">in the manner explained regarding the Jewish people,</t>
    <t s="3">because of a spirit of folly that enters him and covers and conceals the truth, which contradicts that which is called Eloka d'Elokaya.</t>
    <t s="4">But from their own perspective, as they are influenced from the kelipos and sitra achra, they are in a manner that they will not transgress and will not rebel,</t>
    <t s="5">and like Bilaam who said, "I cannot transgress the word of Hashem"</t>
    <t s="6">(see Tanya ch. 24),</t>
    <t s="7">even though he came upon his donkey</t>
    <t s="8">(<a href="/library/article_cdo/aid/5458666/jewish/page.</t>
    <t s="9">htm" data-book-id="17216-5458666" title="Sanhedrin 105,</t>
    <t s="10">b" target="_blank">Sanhedrin 105,</t>
    <t s="11">b.</t>
    <t s="12">Zohar I 128,</t>
    <t s="13">b),</t>
    <t s="14">which is from the Seven Noachide Laws.</t>
    <t s="15">Or</t>
    <t s="16">"Because of the greatness and intensity of their iniquity" their heart rules over their mind</t>
    <t s="17">(in the manner explained regarding the Jewish people – Tanya ch. 17),</t>
    <t s="18">even though this is the opposite of the natural outcome also in a Noachide</t>
    <t s="19">(see Tanya ch. 51).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
